title: Purification and characterization of different proteasome species from mammalian cells
protocol: Grow and expand A549-PSMD14-HTBH cells that stably express proteasome subunit, PSMD14 which has a tandem 6× his and biotin tag.
Prepare 10 mL of Lysis buffer and 40 mL of washing buffer.
Remove all cell culture media from the 150-mm cell culture plates.
Add ∼10 mL of PBS onto the plate to completely remove media.
Remove PBS from the plates.
Add 1 mL of ice-cold Lysis buffer per plate and immediately scrape the cells off the plates.
Transfer detached cells to a 15-mL Dounce tissue grinder.
Lyse the cells by gently moving the Dounce tissue grinder up and down about 15 times.
Transfer the buffer which has lysed cells into multiple 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tubes, maximum 1 mL at a time.
Centrifuge the tubes at 16,000× g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Insert the same number of new 1.5-mL microcentrifuge tubes into a magnetic rack.
Transfer 100 μL of streptavidin magnetic beads (50% slurry) to each tube.
Add 1 mL of ice-cold washing buffer to each tube.
Resuspend the magnetic beads after removing the tubes from the magnetic rack.
Insert the tubes back into the magnetic rack.
Remove all the buffer once the beads are completely gathered onto the magnet.
Repeat steps of adding and removing washing buffer two more times.
Prevent the beads from drying out by quickly adding washing buffer when removing it during bead washing.
Add supernatants from whole A549-PSMD14-HTBH cell lysates to the washed beads.
Incubate tubes in a tube rotator overnight at 4°C.
Prepare 40 mL of washing buffer, 10 mL of TEV washing buffer, and 5 mL of TEV protease buffer.
Remove all supernatant from the tubes containing beads.
Wash the streptavidin magnetic beads with ice-cold washing buffer.
Insert the tubes into the magnetic rack.
Remove all the buffer after beads are completely gathered onto the magnet.
Repeat steps two times.
Wash the streptavidin magnetic beads once with TEV washing buffer.
Add 500 μL of TEV protease buffer to the tube.
Incubate the tubes for 2 h at 30°C in a water bath.
Gently invert the tubes every 30 minutes for resuspension.
Prepare Amicon Ultra-0.5 centrifugal filter units and place them into microcentrifuge tubes.
Transfer supernatants to Amicon filter units after beads are completely gathered onto the magnet.
Centrifuge the Amicon tubes with samples at 14,000× g for 15 min at 4°C.
Place the Amicon filter device upside down in a clean microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the tubes at 1,000× g for 2 min at 4°C to collect the samples.
Measure the concentration of collected purified proteasomes through BCA assay.
Prepare 200 mL of ice-cold Native gel running buffer.
Assemble a NuPAGE 3–8% Tris-Acetate Protein Gels into an Invitrogen mini-gel tank.
Mix purified proteasomes with 2× Native sample buffer (Novex Tris-Glycine Native Sample Buffer).
Wash each well of the native gel using a 5-mL syringe.
Load 1–2 μg of purified proteasomes to a well.
Run samples for 4 h at 150 V at 4°C.
Prepare 15 mL of In-gel activity assay buffer.
Take the gel from the pre-cast cassette and place it in 15 mL of In-gel activity assay buffer.
Incubate the gel in the In-gel activity assay buffer for 10 minutes at 37°C, protected from light.
Spray ddH2O onto the gel to prevent drying.
Place the gel on a ChemiDoc imaging system (ChemiDoc MP Imaging System).
Detect the AMC signal using the EtBr channel.
Adjust exposure time between 1 and 10 seconds for optimal images of 26S and 30S proteasomes.
Incubate the gel in 0.02% SDS in the In-gel activity assay buffer to open pores of the 20S proteasome.
Add 24 μL of 10% SDS (w/v, in ddH2O) to 12 mL of In-gel activity assay buffer.
Incubate the gel for 10 minutes at 37°C, protected from light.
Place the gel on a ChemiDoc imaging system and detect the AMC signal again.
Spray ddH2O before placing the gel on the ChemiDoc.
Place the gel on the ChemiDoc.
Spray 3 mL of In-gel activity assay buffer containing 0.02% SDS evenly over the gel.
Adjust the exposure time between 1 – 10 s to find the optimal image of 20S proteasomes.
Carefully wash the native gel with ddH2O after detecting the AMC signals.
Activate the PVDF membrane by wetting it in absolute methanol for 10 min.
Assemble the transfer cassette and transfer it in a mini-gel tank for 70 min at 100 V.
Block the PVDF membrane in 2% BSA in TBS-T solution.
Make an antibody solution by diluting the primary antibodies with a 2% BSA in TBS-T solution at 1:1000.
Bind the membrane with antibody cocktails and incubate it on a rocking shaker overnight at 4°C.
Wash the membrane with TBS-T solution for 10 min. Repeat this three times.
Make an antibody solution by diluting the secondary antibody conjugated with HRP with a 2% BSA in TBS-T solution at 1:10000.
Bind the membrane with secondary antibody cocktails and incubate it on a rocking shaker for 1 h at RT.
Wash the membrane with TBS-T solution for 10 min. Repeat this three times.
Incubate the sample as required.
Place the membrane on a gel imaging system after incubation.
Spray ECL solution onto the membrane.
Detect the chemiluminescence signal.
Prepare 15 mL of Proteasome activity assay buffer.
Set up the fluorometer machine (Tecan Infinite M200 Fluorometer) in advance.
Monitor proteasome activity kinetically by measuring the AMC signal for about an hour.
Add 8.33 μL of suc-LLVY-AMC (20 mM) to 12 mL of Proteasome activity assay buffer.
Mix proteasome samples containing 20S, 26S, and 30S with Proteasome activity assay buffer lacking suc-LLVY-AMC at a final concentration of 100 nM.
Add 10 μL of proteasome samples to each well of the 96-well black bottom plate.
Dispense 90 μL of Proteasome activity assay buffer with suc-LLVY-AMC into wells containing samples.
Place the 96-well plate on the fluorometer machine and start measuring proteasome activity.
Save the file in an Excel format after the activity measurement is finished.
Prepare size-exclusion chromatography buffer.
Clean and remove bubbles from the ÄKTA machine's pump, lines, and capillary loop.
Filter all solutions used in the ÄKTA machine through a 0.2 μM membrane filter.
Connect Superose 6 Increase 10/300 GL columns to the ÄKTA properly.
Equilibrate the connected column with ddH2O followed by size-exclusion chromatography buffer.
Turn on Unicorn7 software and enter the protocol.
Inject the sample into the ÄKTA machine.
Using a 1 mL syringe, draw up purified proteasome samples to 1 mL.
Invert the syringe and gently tap it to remove bubbles.
Inject the sample into the capillary loop through the injection port.
Prepare approximately 100 of 1.5-mL tubes and place them on the fractionation collector.
If not using the protein eluates immediately, add 50 μL of 50% glycerol to each tube.
Move collected protein eluates to ice every 5 minutes during fractionation.
Snap-freeze samples with liquid nitrogen if not analyzing immediately.
Store fractionated samples at -80°C for long-term storage.
Subject the fractionated samples to SDS-PAGE followed by immunoblotting using various proteasome subunit antibodies.
Add Denaturation buffer to proteasome samples.
Vortex and spin down the tubes.
Sonicate the samples using a water bath sonicator.
Vortex and spin down the tubes again.
Boil the samples for 15 min at 95°C.
After cooling at RT, spin down the tubes.
Add 300 μL Urea buffer to the denatured samples.
Vortex and spin down the tubes.
Transfer the samples to Amicon Ultra-0.5 centrifugal filter units.
Centrifuge samples at 14,000× g for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the flow-through from the collection tubes.
Add 400 μL of urea buffer to the filter.
Centrifuge at 14,000× g for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the flow-through from the collection tubes.
Repeat the previous two steps twice.
Add 200 μL of alkylation buffer to the filters.
Incubate in a dark place for 30 minutes.
Centrifuge at 14,000× g for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the flow-through from the collection tubes.
Add 400 μL of urea buffer to the filter.
Centrifuge at 14,000× g for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the flow-through from the collection tubes.
Repeat the previous two steps twice.
Add 400 μL of ABC buffer to the filter.
Centrifuge at 14,000× g for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the flow-through from the collection tubes.
Repeat the previous two steps twice.
Add 100 μL of ABC buffer and 10 μL of trypsin buffer to the filter.
Incubate on a thermomixer at 650 rpm for 16 hours at 37°C.
Centrifuge the digested peptides in the collection tube from the filter unit at 14,000× g for 15 minutes.
Add 100 μL of ABC buffer to the filter.
Centrifuge at 14,000× g for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Add 50 μL of ABC buffer to the filter.
Centrifuge at 14,000× g for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Add 50 μL of NaCl buffer to the filter.
Centrifuge at 14,000× g for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Transfer the digested peptides from the collection tubes to low-retention microcentrifuge tubes.
Prepare StageTip with a triple-layered SDB-RPS disk plug using 200 μL low-retention tips.
Add 150 μL methanol to StageTip and centrifuge at 850× g for 30 s. Discard the flow-through. Repeat twice.
Add 150 μL ACN to StageTip and centrifuge at 850× g for 30 s. Discard the flow-through. Repeat twice.
Equilibrate the column by adding 100 μL Washing buffer (MS) and centrifuge at 850× g for 30 s. Discard the flow-through. Repeat three times.
Acidify the samples with Acidification buffer to a pH of 2 to 3 range.
Transfer the acidified samples to StageTip and centrifuge at 850× g for 30 s.
Wash the column by adding 100 μL Washing buffer (MS) and centrifuge at 850× g for 30 s. Discard the flow-through. Repeat five times.
Elute the desalted peptides into Protein LoBind microcentrifuge tubes using E1 buffer.
Add 40 μL E2 buffer to StageTip.
Elute into a tube using a syringe that fits the tip diameter.
Repeat elution twice.
Dry desalted samples in a CentriVap Benchtop Centrifugal Vacuum Concentrator.
Resuspend dried samples with Sample injection buffer for injection onto the liquid chromatography system.
Add 8 μL of Sample injection buffer to the dried sample.
Vortex sample and spin down the tubes.
Sonicate the samples using a water bath sonicator for 1 min.
Vortex sample again.
Centrifuge at 21,000× g for 1 h at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to LCMS Certified vials.
Inject 3 μL of samples onto LC-MS/MS system for analysis.
Analyze the acquired MS data with MaxQuant software package version 1.6.1.0.
Download the human UniProt FASTA database (2014.12, 88,657 entries), common contaminant database, and iRT database.
Upload the raw file in the Raw data tab.
Set experiments for each sample using the ‘Set Experiment’ function.
Click “Label-free quantification” in the Group-specific parameters tab.
Change “None” to “LFQ”.
Click “Sequence” in the Global parameters tab.
Upload the FASTA file and check the identifier rule corresponding to the UniProt identifier.
Set the Min. peptide length to 6.
Check the iBAQ parameter to conduct data analysis using iBAQ values.
Adjust the “Number of threads” based on your computer’s capabilities.
Start the MQ analysis.
Export the results in text format (proteingroup.txt) or as a spreadsheet for further processing.
